cands.name: Michelle Salzman
cands.bio: Republican state representative for House District 1 (northern Escambia County) since November 2020; Army veteran and businesswoman; raised in Pensacola; re-elected 2022 and 2024.
cands.local_ties: Raised in Pensacola; attended Pensacola State College and University of West Florida (per Wikipedia). FL DOE filing address is in Escambia County.

record.text: Elected in 2020 after defeating incumbent Mike Hill in the Republican primary; re-elected 2022 (primary rematch vs. Hill) and 2024. Served on House Appropriations and Health committees (2023 list).
Co-sponsored HB 543 (2023), the constitutional (permitless) carry bill, which passed both chambers and was signed April 3, 2023.

money_notes.text: Wikipedia, summarizing news coverage of a 2024 Florida Department of State campaign-expenditure audit, notes contributions of $47,500 from the law firm founded by Fred Levin and $20,890.25 from the Lewis Bear Company alcohol distributorship.

controversies.text: 2023: after Rep. Angie Nixon asked on the House floor how many dead Palestinians would be enough, Salzman said "all of them"; she first denied saying it, then said her remark was support for Israel and its right to self-defense (as summarized on Wikipedia).
2024: Florida Department of State notified her that campaign expenditures totaling several thousand dollars were being audited for irregularities (outcome not found).
2021: Rep. Omari Hardy accused her of calling Rep. Webster Barnaby the chamber's "token Black Republican"; she denied it ("an absolute lie").

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.
The 2025-26 General Appropriations Act (state budget), final vote.
Immigration enforcement bill from the 2025 special session: state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Post-hurricane emergency management bill that also limits local governments' ability to adopt stricter development rules after storms.
Online Protections for Minors: restricts social media accounts for minors.
Interests of foreign countries: restricts land purchases near military sites and critical infrastructure by people from China and other 'countries of concern'.
Education: expands school voucher eligibility to all Florida K-12 students.
Heartbeat Protection Act: bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.
Public Safety: lets most adults carry a concealed firearm without a permit (permitless carry).
Property Insurance: creates the Florida Optional Reinsurance Assistance program (FORA) for insurers.
Building Safety (condo safety response after Surfside).
